summary: Clearwater County, Idaho pole lookout on Armstrong Peak, built 1934 and rebuilt 1953; gone since 1962, when sources disagree on removal versus destruction.

facts.design: 60-foot pole tower with L-6 cab and cabin
facts.status_note: Gone since 1962; sources differ on whether it was removed or destroyed

events.note: 60-foot pole tower with L-6 cab and cabin
Association 1953 annual report says the tower was completely rebuilt that year
Association combined 1961-62 report says it was removed in the fall after the fire season
firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts list it as destroyed in 1962

evidence.supports: location 14 miles east of Elk River
built 1934 as 60-foot pole tower with L-6 cab and cabin
listed under Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association

evidence.quote: Armstrong Lookout tower was completely rebuilt this year

evidence.supports: other towers received minor repairs in 1953
evidence.quote: other towers received minor repair work

evidence.supports: not used for years, poor condition, improved detection methods
evidence.quote: not used for several years and in poor condition along with improved detection methods

evidence.supports: removed in the fall after fire season
evidence.quote: was removed in the Fall after fire season

corrections.why: The association's combined 1961-62 report says the tower was removed in the fall after the fire season; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say destroyed. A human should decide which event to keep.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two listings say destroyed in 1962; the association's combined 1961-62 report says removed in the fall after the fire season. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Removal versus destruction in 1962 is disputed: the association report (quoted on Forest Lookouts) says removed after fire season; two listings say destroyed. The 1934 build and 1953 rebuild come from the Forest Lookouts page, which cites Kresek and association annual reports; those were not read directly. No staffing or fire sources were found, so none are in the story. No source describes the site today. Brief record says '1962 destroyed'; see corrections.
